gaps.sentence: ___ he had studied hard, he failed the exam.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a full clause; due/owing take noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: The flat is spacious and well located; ___, the rent is surprisingly low.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds another supporting point in the same direction.

gaps.sentence: The expedition will go ahead ___ the sponsors confirm the funding.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' = only if, a formal positive condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ a slight delay in Rome, the whole journey went smoothly.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from' sets the delay aside as the only problem.

gaps.sentence: He went back inside, ___ the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the danger' — noun phrase; although needs a clause.

gaps.sentence: Bring a thermos ___ the tea tent closes at noon.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against something happening.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: I know exactly what the risks are. ___, I'm going anyway.
gaps.hint: doing it in spite of risk
